title: Mustard greens, frozen, cooked, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Mustard greens (Brassica juncea) are a leafy vegetable rich in vitamins and minerals. In the frozen form the leaves are blanched, then a small amount of fat is added to improve flavor and texture. The product is ready to eat after reheating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mustard greens belong to the cruciferous family, along with broccoli and cabbage.
The raw leaves have a peppery bite that mellows with heat.
Freezing preserves most of the vitamins, especially vitamin C and carotenoids.
In Asian cuisines mustard greens are common in salads, soups, and stir‑fries.
Adding a little oil enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamin A and carotenoids
items.content: Support vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: An antioxidant that helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Provides folate
items.content: Important for DNA synthesis and cell division, especially during pregnancy.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Cruciferous allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to mustard greens.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: High oxalate levels can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: Added fat
items.content: The product contains added fat, so those monitoring calorie intake should account for it.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reheat mustard greens in the microwave or a skillet, add them to soups, stews, pasta dishes, or use as a filling for wraps. They pair well with rice, quinoa, and legumes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen product in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once thawed, consume within 2–3 days and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
